 bd Lakshman Prasad Agarwal
 Vs.
 Union of India & Ors.

Mr. Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharyya, Mr. R. A. Agarwal, Mr. Kumar Gupta, Mr. Rajesh Gupta, Mrs.
Nibedita Pal, Mr. Ramesh Dhara.
... For Petitioner Mr. Rudro Chatterjee ...
For the Respondent Nos. 2 & 3.
Mr. K. K. Maiti.
The petitioner has imported wet dates.

The consignment was put through Customs control, which by an examination order dated 18th May, 2015 recorded, inter alia, that assessment and examination has not been prescribed for the bill of entry while stating the compulsory compliance requirements to be fulfilled.

The Government of India, Ministry of Agriculture, Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine &
Storage by its order dated 19th May, 2015 recommended for release (for consumption purpose only)
the consignment.

Storage

sentences.text: The authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 by its communication dated 20th May, 2015 informed that the concerned bill of entry does not bear the complete name and address of the manufacturer, which is in violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2.6 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: According to them as it was a non rectifiable defect and sample was not drawn.
Mr. Bhattacharyya, learned senior advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that his client is the packer and not the manufacturer.
He further submits that wet dates cannot be manufactured.
He relies on Section 27 of the said Act.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and the Customs Authorities are represented.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: They vehemently opposed any interim order being made regarding drawing of samples while the contentious issue of whether the importer is the manufacturer or a packer is deliberated upon.

sentences.text: Mr. Chatterjee, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent nos. 2 and 3 has relied upon a decision in the case of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India vs. Heartland Trading Company Pvt. Ltd. & Others reported in 2014 SCC OnLine Cal 19348 to draw attention of this Court to the following views expressed in that judgment.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India vs. Heartland Trading Company Pvt. Ltd. & Others reported in 2014 SCC OnLine Cal 19348
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "It is not the law that if the imported food articles are found to be safe and wholesome for human consumption, then the Food Authority is bound to grant Heartland NOC, even if their labelling does not fulfil the requirements of the regulations.
Such a proposition shall defeat the provisions of s. 23 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and make the provisions of the regulations otios.
Purpose of labelling is not to be ascertained by anyone for diluting the rigours of the regulations and importing the concept of substantial compliance therewith.
It is not that validity of any provision is in issue.
Strict compliance principle seems to be the requirements of the regulations dictated by public interest that must prevail over any private interest of an importer."
It appears from the judgment relied upon that the matter of requirements regarding labelling must be complied with strictly.
That would determine the fate for grant of Heartland NOC irrespective of whether the imported food articles are found to be safe or not.

The goods, being food articles and perishable in nature, this Court is of the view that within the time taken to determine whether there has been strict compliance in the matter regarding labelling, the exercise of finding out whether the goods are fit for human consumption must be completed.
That should not be kept pending.

In the circumstances, there will an order directing the concerned respondents to draw and test samples in terms of the said Act and Regulations framed thereunder, the exercise to be completed within 5th June, 2015.
Let this matter be listed as per the convenience of the regular Bench.
Liberty to mention for early listing.

(Arindam Sinha, J.)
